title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X is smooth projective of dimension n over an algebraically closed field. A_X is the Albanese variety. B_X is the Picard variety Pic^0, carrying the Poincaré divisor class D in Cl(X x B_X). There are two maps:
- Phi_X : H^1(A_X,Q_l) -> H^1(X,Q_l), induced by the Albanese map. It is an isomorphism and is given by an algebraic correspondence (the graph).
- Psi_X : H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1) -> H^1(B_X,Q_l), induced by the Poincaré divisor. It is an isomorphism and is algebraic.

The goal, part of proving '2.7' in this special case, is to show that Psi_X^{-1} and Phi_Y^{-1} are also induced by algebraic cycles with Q coefficients, independently of l. On the previous page this was used to show that an isogeny B_X -> A_Y comes from a 1-cycle Z on X x Y whose class inverts a(gamma(D)).

On this page Grothendieck picks a polarisation xi in A^1(X) and forms a commutative square:
- lambda = cup with xi^{n-1}, from H^1(X) to H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). This is hard Lefschetz in degree 1, an isomorphism, and is algebraic.
- mu : H^1(A_X) -> H^1(B_X) is induced by the isogeny between Albanese and Picard determined by the polarisation (via 2.6).
- The square commutes: mu = Psi_X o lambda o Phi_X.

Hence Psi_X^{-1} = lambda o Phi_X o mu^{-1}. Here mu^{-1} is algebraic because a Q-isogeny has an inverse in Hom ⊗ Q, which is realised by the graph of a quasi-inverse isogeny divided by its degree. So Psi_X^{-1} is algebraic.

Symmetrically, Phi_X^{-1} = mu^{-1} o Psi_X o lambda is algebraic. Applying this to Y gives Phi_Y^{-1}.

Conclusion: in degree 1, the inverses of the Lefschetz-type and Albanese/Picard isomorphisms are algebraic with Q coefficients. This is the classical fact that the Lefschetz standard conjecture holds for H^1, obtained by reducing to abelian varieties and isogenies.

The next page asks whether these inverses can be realised by integral cycles. That reduces to whether the generic fibre of Sym^m X -> A_X has a rational point, and to the integral question for abelian varieties.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument implicitly uses that mu is an isomorphism, i.e. that the polarisation-induced map between A_X and B_X is an isogeny. That is a nondegeneracy statement equivalent to hard Lefschetz on H^1, presumably what is cited as 2.6.
The direction of Phi_X in the diagram is ambiguous: the arrow is drawn double-headed. The formulas are consistent only if Phi_X : H^1(A_X) -> H^1(X), i.e. mu = Psi_X lambda Phi_X.

ideas.what: Algebraicity of the inverse of hard Lefschetz and of the Albanese/Picard identifications on H^1, by reducing to inverting an isogeny of abelian varieties.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) / A(X) in degree 1 (Lieberman-Kleiman); divisorial correspondences vs. homomorphisms Pic^0 -> Alb
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's 1969 'Standard conjectures' remarks; Lieberman (1968); Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968), where degree 1 is proved via abelian varieties; classical Weil theory of correspondences
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/1969) mentions the known low-degree cases; full proof written by Kleiman (Dix exposés 1968)

ideas.what: Using a polarisation to identify H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) with H^1(X) and the Picard variety with the Albanese up to isogeny.
ideas.modern_name: Polarisation isogeny Alb_X -> Pic^0_X induced by xi^{n-1}

missed.claim: Nothing new on this page itself; it is a clean write-up of the known degree-1 case. The only point of potential interest is on the next page: Grothendieck asks for integral versions, i.e. integral cycles inverting H(A_X) -> H(X). He links this to the generic fibre of Sym^m X -> A_X having a rational point. This anticipates later work on integral Hodge/Tate questions and universal 1-cycles (e.g. Voisin, Colliot-Thélène). These were reached independently.
missed.quote: μ est défini par une Q-isogénie B_X → A_X ..., dont on peut prendre l'inverse
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This page only marks why Q coefficients are needed: the inverse of an isogeny is not integral. That motivates the integral questions raised on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: A standard and correct argument (algebraicity of Lefschetz inverses in degree 1 via isogenies), already in Kleiman/Lieberman and alluded to in Grothendieck's standard conjectures paper.
transcription_corrections: 'H^{2n-i}(X,Q_l)(n-i)' should read H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1); likewise 'H^i' should read H^1 and 'cup ξ^{n-i}' should read cup ξ^{n-1}.
The parenthetical under the diagram is partly struck out. It appears to read '(μ étant défini comme ψ_X λ φ_X [or ψ_X λ φ_X^{-1}] ... et de 2.6.)'.
'donc on est ramené à trouver[?] que "algébrique"' is better read as 'donc on est ramené à prouver μ^{-1} "algébrique"'.
'(où on peut remplacer X par Y)' is plausibly '(où on peut remplacer Y par X)', which matches the sense.
